RAF Cosford Air Show

The Royal Air Force’s own air show. One Sunday in June, ticket only

Cosford is the only air show run by the RAF itself, on a working station next to the RAF Museum Midlands. It’s a one day show with the Red Arrows, the Typhoon, the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight and visiting warbirds flying over a proper airfield crowd line. On the ground you get a big static park, STEM and engineering hangars, the museum and plenty for children to do.

2027 date to be confirmedThe RAF Cosford Air Show is normally held on the second Sunday in June, which would be 13 June 2027. The 2026 show sold out in advance. Tickets for 2027 haven’t gone on sale yet, so the details here are based on the 2026 show until the organisers announce more.

The show at a glance

Cosford is a one day, ticket only show on an RAF station in Shropshire, a few miles from Wolverhampton and Telford. Around 50,000 people come, and in 2026 every ticket went before the day. Nothing is sold at the gate.

What makes Cosford different is that the RAF runs it. The flying display is built around the RAF’s own teams, with the Red Arrows, the Typhoon Display Team, the Falcons parachute team and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, plus visiting warbirds like the B-17 Sally B. Gates open at 08:00 and the flying starts late morning, so you have a few hours to look around the static park and the hangars first.

On the ground there’s a lot to see. The static display sits on the airfield in front of the crowd line, the museum hangars are open, and the STEM and engineering areas are aimed at families and anyone thinking about a career in the RAF. It works well for a mixed group, as long as everyone is happy to be on an airfield for the day.

The main things to plan for are buying your tickets early, the queues on the A41 and at Cosford station, and the fact that it is a one day event, so if the weather is poor there is no second chance. I would advise arriving as the gates open, and if you are coming by car, parking is included in your ticket.

The RAF Village

This is the RAF’s own show, so the RAF Village is bigger here than anywhere else. It’s a great way for your kids to learn about and explore the different roles in the RAF, and if anyone in your group would like to join the RAF, it’s the place to ask any questions they may have.

You’ll also see many of the RAF display teams on the ground, like the famous Red Arrows pilots and their ground crew, where kids can get stickers and take photos with the pilots. The RAF Typhoon Display Team, the Black Cats and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight are often there too.

    Our view

    If you want to see the RAF at its own show, Cosford is the one. You get the Red Arrows, the Typhoon and the Memorial Flight on a real airfield, a static park you can walk around and the museum next door, all for one ticket with the parking included. Buy your tickets the day they go on sale, arrive as the gates open and plan a slow exit.

    RAF Cosford Air ShowParking & arrival guide

    Cosford is unusual: the railway station is right next to the airfield, under 300 metres from the entrance, and parking on the airfield is included in your ticket. The catch is that everyone arrives on the same morning, so the A41 and the M54 queue and the station gets very busy. I would advise the train if you can manage steps, or arriving by car as the gates open at 08:00.

    Ways to arrive

    Based on the 2026 show. Train services, road closures and parking for 2027 are still to be confirmed.

    Do I need a ticket?
    Yes, for everyone over 16, and only in advance. Nothing is sold at the gates and the 2026 show sold out. Under 16s go free with a paying adult, but you must say how many children are coming when you book. Tickets are non refundable and non transferable, and the only official resale is through See Tickets.
    Is parking really included?
    Yes. Parking on the airfield is included in the admission price. It is on grass, so vehicles must be no longer than 7 metres and under 7.5 tonnes. You can’t be dropped off at the airfield itself. The nearest drop-off point is the BP garage on the A41.
    Which roads close?
    In 2026 Newport Road in Albrighton by the fire station and at the junction with the A41, Rectory Road, Green Lane, Bowling Green Lane and Kennel Lane were closed from 07:00 to 17:30. Residents kept access, but there was no public parking, waiting or viewing on those roads. The A41 and A464 next to the airfield are clearways on show day, so you can’t stop or park on them.
    Which gate do I use?
    Follow the air show signs rather than your satnav once you see them. In 2026 Gate 4 was open for arrivals from about 08:00 to 10:00 and for departures from about 18:00, and the one way system usually reverses around 13:00 so you can leave through Gate 2.
    Can I use the train if I can’t manage steps?
    Cosford station has no disabled access, so the organisers can’t recommend it if you are unable to manage steps. The disabled car park is the better option: follow the wheelchair signs and display your Blue Badge. Spaces are limited and first come first served.
    Can I bring my bike or motorbike?
    Yes, there is parking for both at the airfield, but security is your own responsibility.

    Where to stay

    RAF Cosford sits between Wolverhampton and Telford, so most beds are in those two towns, in Shifnal and Albrighton next door, or in Bridgnorth and the Ironbridge Gorge a little further out. It is a one day show, but with 50,000 visitors the nearest rooms go early, so I would advise booking as soon as the date is confirmed.

    Pick your spot

    The crowd line runs along the north side of runway 06/24, so you look south east across the runway with the display line beyond it. What changes is where you are along the line, how much space you get, and how near the static park, food and toilets are.

    Filter by feature

    Shooting at Cosford

    The crowd line faces south south east across runway 06/24, so you’re shooting into the sun around the middle of the day and it swings round behind your right shoulder through the afternoon. Displays are close in over the runway, so 300 to 500mm is plenty.

    Get creative on the airfield

    Cosford is kinder to photographers than a seafront show. The displays are close, there is a runway for take offs, landings and taxiing shots, and the hangars and control tower give you a background that says RAF. The crowd line faces towards the sun for much of the day, so I would suggest using the sun guide to plan your close up work for the afternoon, and spending the morning on the static park and the arrivals.

    Ideas to try

    • Shoot the take offs and landings. Heat haze off the runway softens things on a hot day, so get them early or wait for the climb out.
    • Wait for the banking passes at the 06 end. A topside view shows far more of the aircraft than a straight flypast.
    • Leave room in the frame for the Red Arrows’ smoke, so it leads the eye to the aircraft.
    • Zoom out now and then to include the hangars, the tower or the crowd, so the photo says Cosford.
    • Walk the static park before 10:00 for clean shots without the crowds.

    Starting settings

    Pick what’s flying and the weather for a starting point. It never goes faster than 1/2000 or above ISO 1200, so the files stay clean and the shutter stays realistic for the subject. Check your histogram after the first pass and adjust.

    Food, toilets & access

    Everything is on the airfield, so plan to eat, drink and rest on site. You can bring your own food and drink, and there is a food village, but there is no town to pop out to and the queues peak at lunchtime.

    Food & drink

    A catering village with hot and cold food, plus stalls across the showground. Picnics are welcome but cooking equipment isn’t allowed. Queues peak around lunchtime, so eat a little earlier or later, and bring cash in case the card machines lose signal.

    Kids’ activities

    The STEM and engineering hangars, simulators, the static park and the RAF Village keep younger visitors busy between displays, and the museum next door is free.

    Toilets

    Toilet blocks across the showground with baby changing next to them, and disabled toilets by the disabled car park. Go before the flying starts, and if you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use that slot as your break.

    Shade and seating

    There is almost no shade on the crowd line, so bring hats, sun cream and your own chairs. Gazebos aren’t allowed on the crowd line, but small shelters are fine further back.

    Accessibility
    The showground is flat but mostly grass, and it is a long walk from the car parks. A disabled car park sits close to the showground, first come first served, and Event Mobility Charitable Trust provides electric scooters and manual wheelchairs to book in advance. Qualifying adults can bring a registered carer free. Cosford station has no step-free access.
    What can I bring?
    Folding chairs, picnic blankets, food and drink. No cooking equipment, no gazebos on the crowd line, no drones within six miles of the airfield and no pets other than assistance dogs. Smoking and vaping aren’t allowed on the showground.
    Programme
    The souvenir programme was £10 in 2026 and is the only place the flying times are published, so it is worth buying one on the way in.
    Medical help
    Treatment facilities are across the site. Ask any steward and they will point you to the nearest one.
    The museum
    RAF Museum Midlands sits on the same site, with free entry. Its hangars are the best shade on a hot day, and it is a good place for the children to cool off between displays.
    If the weather turns
    Low cloud or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. It is a one day show with no fall back, so check the official channels on the morning and pack a waterproof.
